---
title: "Reproducible R"
subtitle: "Preserve the data, decisions, code, outputs and environment needed to recreate an analysis."
---

## Reproducibility is a chain

::: {.reasoning-loop}
Question → Source data → Eligibility → Preparation → Analysis → Diagnostics → Results → Interpretation → Decision
:::

If any link is missing, a final number may be impossible to recreate or explain.

## Project structure

```text
project/
├── analysis.qmd
├── data/
│   └── source-data.csv
├── R/
│   └── helper-functions.R
├── figures/
└── outputs/
```

Use relative paths such as `data/source-data.csv`. Keep original data read-only and generate derived outputs through code.

## A reproducible document

Quarto or R Markdown can contain:

- the research question;
- prose explaining decisions;
- executable code;
- generated tables and figures;
- interpretation beside output;
- citations and limitations.

Run the document from top to bottom in a clean session. Code that only works because an object was created manually in the console is not reproducible.

## Record data provenance

Document:

- dataset name, source and version;
- date obtained or generated;
- unit of observation;
- data dictionary;
- inclusion and exclusion criteria;
- transformations and derived variables;
- missing-data handling;
- linkage or deduplication decisions.

## Control randomness

```r
set.seed(2026)
training_rows <- sample(
  seq_len(nrow(analysis_data)),
  size = floor(0.8 * nrow(analysis_data))
)
```

Set the seed immediately before the random operation it is intended to reproduce. Record the split rule as well as the seed.

## Preserve analytical decisions

Record choices that code alone may not explain:

- why variables entered a model;
- reference categories;
- outcome definitions and time horizons;
- transformations;
- thresholds;
- planned contrasts;
- sensitivity analyses;
- deviations from a protocol.

## Record the software environment

```r
sessionInfo()
```

For more formal work, dependency management tools such as `renv` can record package versions. The appropriate approach depends on the assessment or project infrastructure.

## Export deliberately

```r
write_csv(results_table, "outputs/results-table.csv")
saveRDS(adjusted_model, "outputs/adjusted-model.rds")
ggsave("figures/primary-outcome.png", plot = primary_plot)
```

Reopen exported files and confirm they contain the expected rows, columns, labels and values.

## The final reproducibility check

- [ ] The clinical question and estimand are explicit.
- [ ] Source data remain unchanged.
- [ ] Eligibility and missingness are quantified.
- [ ] Every result is generated by visible code.
- [ ] Important outputs have meaningful object names.
- [ ] Random operations have recorded seeds.
- [ ] Model assumptions and sensitivity analyses are documented.
- [ ] Tables and figures are generated, not manually transcribed.
- [ ] Software versions are available.
- [ ] The document runs in a clean session.
- [ ] Exported files have been reopened and checked.
- [ ] Identifiable data are stored and shared only through approved systems.

::: {.clinical-lens}
Reproducibility does not guarantee validity. Another analyst can perfectly reproduce a biased design or an inappropriate model. The goal is to make both the result and the reasoning inspectable.
:::
